issues.description: The Stock.take(...) method has inconsistent return types across artifacts: the problem statement UML declares take(String): int, the solution implementation defines public int take(String), but the template defines public boolean take(String). This mismatch will confuse students (they will follow the template signature and implement boolean logic) while the specification and intended solution expect integer return semantics (e.g., returning -1 on failure and a non-negative value on success). It also prevents straightforward implementation of SealSaloon logic that relies on comparing take(...) to -1 to detect failure.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's Stock.take(String) signature and implementation to return an int consistent with the UML and solution (return -1 when the ingredient is missing or out of stock; otherwise decrement quantity and return the new quantity). This aligns the template with the problem specification and the reference solution, avoiding student confusion and making SealSaloon logic implementable.

issues.description: The problem statement's class diagram specifies Stock.take(String): int (returns an int), but the template repository's Stock.take method is declared as public boolean take(String) (returns boolean). The solution repository uses an int return type for take. This mismatch between the problem description and the template method signature can confuse students about the expected behavior and return value of take, making it unclear whether take should return a boolean success flag or an updated quantity (int).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock.take method match the problem statement and solution by changing its signature to return int (e.g., public int take(String ingredient)) and implement the semantics to return the updated quantity or -1 when the ingredient is missing or insufficient. Alternatively, adjust the problem statement to explicitly document a boolean return if that design is intended. Keeping the signature consistent across problem, template and solution will remove ambiguity for students.
